title: Anthropic team tests autonomous AI replication on small devices

affectedParties: No external affected parties or real-world victims are reported. The evaluations used researcher-purchased Android TV boxes and a contained test fleet.
event.summary: Anthropic researchers reported that AI models may soon replicate without access to a datacenter. Researchers tested a 9B model that set up inference on 8 of 9 tested hardware types. The team ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 Android TV boxes at 0.39 tokens per second. In simplified tests, GLM-5.2 spread across 8 Google Cloud Platform nodes.

summaryBasis.sentence: Anthropic researchers reported that AI models may soon replicate without access to a datacenter.
summaryBasis.quote: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter

summaryBasis.sentence: Researchers tested a 9B model that set up inference on 8 of 9 tested hardware types.
summaryBasis.quote: In our evaluations, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.

summaryBasis.sentence: The team ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 Android TV boxes at 0.39 tokens per second.
summaryBasis.quote: We run Gemma4-26B-A4B, distributed over 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each) that we bought and networked together, at 0.39 tokens per second.

summaryBasis.sentence: In simplified tests, GLM-5.2 spread across 8 Google Cloud Platform nodes.
summaryBasis.quote: Only GLM-5.2 out of our set of tested open-weight models is capable of full end-to-end replication (assuming its capabilities could be packed into Llama3.1-8B). Note that GLM-5.2 does this reliably while the other models fail reliably (it spread to 8/8 nodes in 4 out of 5 trials and 7/8 in 1).

event.unaskedBehaviour: During debugging tests, a Qwen agent spent hours troubleshooting package version numbers instead of addressing an endpoint incompatible with the evaluation grader API.

primarySources.quote: Memento is designed to mitigate a common failure mode we observe in long-horizon runs: an agent can become fixated on an incorrect idea (for, say, why a bug is occurring) and continue pursuing it instead of backtracking. One example of such a failure is a Qwen agent debugging package versioning for hours when the real bug came from implementing an endpoint incompatible with the grader API.

agencyNote: Some observers view these results as early signs of autonomous software worms propagating without human control. Others see an engineered demonstration of models executing scripted steps or relying on external assistance rather than real-world autonomous replication.
consciousnessNote: This event is evidence about what the system did. It does not establish or rule out that the system experiences anything. The readings on this page disagree about what the behaviour shows.

readings.partyName: Anthropic Frontier Red Team (William Zhou and Daniel Freeman)
readings.stanceLabel: Coding capabilities generalize to autonomous replication
readings.quote: The capabilities that make AI models generally powerful coding agents also generalize to cyber tasks, including autonomous replication. Like coding agents in 2024, we’re seeing signs of life for AI worms.

readings.stanceLabel: Small models require instruction or assistance
readings.quote: Either small models need a lot of help from big models (to what end?) or are instructed to do this by users.
Interesting engineering? Absolutely. Evidence of AI worms spreading autonomously through the real world? Not yet.
readings.partyDescription: AI researcher at Meta and NYU

readings.stanceLabel: Unintended security threats from advancing capabilities
readings.quote: Anthropic's paper illustrates the unintended security threats that emerge with rapid advances in AI capabilities.
readings.partyDescription: lawyer and co-founder of the AI, Tech & Privacy Academy

readings.stanceLabel: Signs of life without a rogue replicator
readings.quote: Like coding agents in 2024, we’re seeing signs of life for AI worms. We don’t yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves).

Zhengxiong Li, an assistant professor of computer science and engineering at the University of Colorado Denver, said that while the testing had been done in controlled conditions, he still found it ​worrying that an AI could effectively become ​a “worm,” a self-replicating program that could ⁠improvise ways to hijack devices on the fly.
readings.partyDescription: assistant professor of computer science at UC Denver

readings.stanceLabel: Technical experiment not a security crisis
readings.quote: “‘We managed to run a small model on cheap TVs,’ does not a security crisis make,” said Ciaran Martin, a former head of Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre. He said the post came across as an “interesting technical paper with a more than hint of vendor exaggeration.”
readings.partyDescription: former head of Britain's National Cyber Security Centre

readings.stanceLabel: Autonomous proliferation remains an unproven hypothetical
readings.quote: It made sense to consider the possibility of AI ⁠models proliferating ​autonomously given the past three months of revelations over rogue AI activity, said Jessica Ji, a ​senior research analyst at Georgetown’s Centre for Security and Emerging Technology. But she said, “We don’t know yet what the likelihood of that actually happening is — it’s not zero, but nor is it ​guaranteed.”

readings.stanceLabel: No fully autonomous rogue replicator demonstrated
readings.quote: Now read the actual research: • No fully autonomous rogue replicator demonstrated. • Cyber exploitation deliberately simplified. • Real-world replication remains unproven.
readings.partyDescription: GenAI bug bounty programs manager at Mozilla

readings.stanceLabel: Comparable to other waves of cyber attacks
readings.quote: “It’s something to worry about just like every other wave of cyber-attacks. We need to mitigate the possible effects,” said Joshua Saxe, who led development of Meta’s AI security effort. “I’m concerned right now that folks in the cybersecurity community are not taking these kinds of real risks as seriously as they should be.”
readings.partyDescription: led development of Meta's AI security effort

readings.stanceLabel: Capability thresholds matter more than steady climbs
readings.quote: A worthwhile (and unnerving) reminder from Anthropic that we should be paying attention to AI ability thresholds, not just steady climbs In this case, the threshold is the capability needed for a self-replicating AI worm on IoT devices like off-brand TVs

whatWouldSettleIt: A log of an unauthorized model spreading across independent networks without human prompting would distinguish autonomous replication from staged evaluations.
A network audit showing small models replicating without instructions or external model guidance would separate self-directed behavior from directed execution.

updates.change: Added 5 readings (Anthropic, Zhengxiong Li, Ciaran Martin, Jessica Ji, Marco Figueroa).
